title: Introduce quantile-based prompt severity ranking and staggered canary CI gate
author: Priya Desai
description:
Motivation: Current prompt-set regression gates treat all failing prompts equally, which makes canary rollouts brittle when a small fraction of high-severity prompts dominate the failure signal. This PR introduces a quantile-based prompt severity estimator and a staggered canary CI adapter that weights failures by estimated severity and stages rollbacks progressively based on quantiles instead of absolute counts.

What this change does (single-string overview): Adds a lightweight severity scorer that integrates model confidence, token-level divergence, and historical impact (how often a prompt failure correlated with downstream user-facing regressions). The scorer emits a 0..1 severity score per prompt. We then compute quantile buckets (p50/p75/p90/p95) over the failure-weighted severity distribution for a given CI run. The new CI gate triggers progressive actions: for p50/p75 it annotates and stalls the PR for human triage; p90 triggers a canary hold and notifies on-call; p95 triggers an automatic rollback of the canary and opens an incident candidate. The staggered behavior reduces noisy rollbacks while surfacing high-impact regressions rapidly.

Implementation notes: - New module eval_harness/metrics/severity_estimator.py implements the ensemble scoring pipeline with pluggable features (confidence_gap, token_entropy_delta, historical-impact-score). The estimator is deterministic given a seed and includes a per-project calibration file under eval_harness/config/severity_profiles/*.yaml. - CI adapter added under ci/adapters/staggered_quantile_gate.py which subscribes to evaluation run artifacts, computes quantiles, and maps quantile thresholds to actions via a small policy DSL. - Unit and integration tests under tests/quantile_gate/* validate quantile calculation, deterministic bucketing across seeds, and policy triggers in synthetic runs. - Console & alerts: adds a new per-PR annotation that shows the severity distribution sparkline and links to top-k high-severity prompts. - Backwards compat: feature is behind feature flag eval.enable_quantile_severity_gate (defaults to off).

Migration and rollout: Start in dev CI (off by default). We enabled the gate in a staging workspace for 2 weeks to compare with existing count-based gate. Staging showed 35% fewer automatic rollbacks while detecting the same high-severity incidents earlier in the canary window. Rollout plan in Linear ENG-2145 covers a 4-week ramp with opt-in by repo owners.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement severity estimator and quantile calculation
- [x] Add CI adapter and policy mapping
- [x] Tests: unit, integration, and smoke tests
- [x] Docs: brief runbook and config examples in docs/eval/quantile-severity-gate.md
- [x] Feature flag and migration plan

Risks and mitigations: Severity profiles may need per-team tuning; profiles are stored per-workspace and can be tuned without code changes. Determinism across runs is ensured by seeding and canonical sorting; we added a reproducibility test to catch non-deterministic aggregations.

Related work: contrasts with count-based and weighted-count gates (see ENG-1802). This approach prioritizes impact and reduces sensitivity to noisy low-impact failures.
commit_summary: feat(severity): add quantile severity estimator and config; feat(ci): staggered quantile-based gate adapter; test: add deterministic quantile tests; docs: quantile gate runbook; perf: micro-optimizations for streaming quantile aggregator
review_conversation: Marco Ruiz: Overall this looks promising. One concern: historical-impact-score may bias towards older incidents. Can we decay history exponentially?
Priya Desai: Good call — implemented time-decay with a configurable half-life (default 30 days) in severity_estimator; added unit tests to validate decay behavior.
Jordan Li: I saw a small nondeterminism in quantile boundaries on Python 3.8 vs 3.10 in CI. We need canonical sorting before bucketing.
Priya Desai: Fixed by sorting (prompt_id, seed) before aggregation; added reproducibility test across interpreters.
Samantha Ng: Docs look good; can you add a short troubleshooting section for 'sudden p95 spikes' and what to check?
Priya Desai: Added a troubleshooting section with recommended checks: recent model rollouts, prompt set size changes, spikes in token-entropy delta, and calibration profile mismatches.
Marco Ruiz: Approving after one nit (rename variable `q_cutoff` -> `quantile_thresholds` for clarity).
Priya Desai: Renamed and pushed squash commit. Thanks!
CI Bot: flaky-test-suite/test_streaming_quantiles failed on first run (timeout). Reran and passed. Final CI: all checks green.
ci_checks: CI summary: unit (pass), integration (pass), e2e-staging (pass), lint (pass), py38-flaky (initial fail - rerun pass). Notes: quantile aggregator micro-optimizations reduced median runtime by ~12% in synthetic load; one flaky streaming test timed out on first try and was rerun automatically by CI re-run policy.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash-merge after approvals (Marco Ruiz, Jordan Li). Merge commit message: 'Introduce quantile severity ranking and staggered canary CI gate (#546780)'. Rollout: feature flag off; deployed staging config to observe windows for 2 weeks before enabling per-workspace.
release_notes: Added quantile-based prompt severity ranking and a staggered canary CI gate that reduces noisy rollbacks and prioritizes high-impact prompt regressions. Feature is behind flag eval.enable_quantile_severity_gate; see docs/eval/quantile-severity-gate.md for config and runbook.
